name: Asymmetric-Two-Form Khronon MOND (ATF-KM)
claimed_mechanism: The theory introduces a propagating khronon u_mu and a degenerate antisymmetric two-form B_mu_nu. The PPN-slip (lensing) response is generated by the u_mu coupling to acceleration, strictly screened by e^-y. Crucially, the kinetic normalization of the u_mu field is NOT controlled by this screened coupling; instead, it is fixed by the independent stiffness term of B_mu_nu (which couples to the curl of u_mu). This geometrically separates the PPN alpha-parameters (screened) from the kinetic mass scale (independent), thereby attacking the P7 collision.
predicted_weak_field: In the Solar System (y >> 1), the e^-y screening suppresses the preferred-frame slip to alpha ~ e^-y, satisfying G7. The lensing potential Phi equals Psi (gamma=1) in the Newtonian limit because the B_mu_nu field is purely spatial and does not source the trace of the metric. In the MOND regime (y << 1), the u_mu field becomes active, generating the necessary off-ray slip to enhance lensing to the MOND level, while the B_mu_nu stiffness ensures the longitudinal mode remains canonical and finite.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-014 (stiff/non-propagating vector) because u_mu is explicitly propagating (standard kinetic term via B_mu_nu), not stiff. It is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the preferred-frame coupling is screened by e^-y (AeST has constant K_B coupling). It is inequivalent to DC-010 (khronometric) because the kinetic normalization is decoupled from the screened PPN coupling via the two-form B_mu_nu, directly addressing the P7 strong-coupling wound that closed the previous khronometric family.
